containers.name: Linux, FEX + bionic, no PRoot (experimental)
containers.description: Shadow of the Tomb Raider, native x86-64 Steam build 11668867, run by Android FEX 2610 (Performance preset) directly, with no PRoot around the game and the Steam client kept on the glibc runtime. Android Vulkan thunks, the Turnip driver the app chooses for the GPU (DD-Turnip v0.1.1 on Adreno 840), native Vulkan output, 2 GB reported GPU budget, 1280x800. The game reaches its menus and gameplay on a RedMagic Astra 2 (Android 16, Adreno 840) and matches the PRoot preset there: 72-75 FPS against 73-75 in the main menu at 1280x720 on the lowest preset, cold start. Turnip builds from DD-Turnip v0.1.1 to Gen8 V38 behave alike; the stock Qualcomm driver crashes the game. The first run after changing the graphics settings compiles shaders and is slow. Needs the app build with the direct FEX bridge for Shadow and its /tmp and /dev/shm path mapping. Long sessions and Steam cloud/overlay behaviour are untested; the PRoot preset is the fallback.

containers.name: BeamNG 0.40 - Linux, FEX + bionic, no PRoot, 960x544
containers.description: BeamNG 0.40.x native Linux build, the configuration measured on West Coast (0.40.4.0): FEX 2610 Performance (TSO off), bionic and direct execution with no PRoot, Vulkan thunks, Turnip driver chosen by the app for the GPU (DD-Turnip v0.1.1 on Adreno 840) for the renderer and the game, native Vulkan output, 960x544 with the app upscaler, post effects and frame generation off, sysmem off, GPU memory 8192 MB. Set BeamNG's own graphics to the Lowest preset with a 960 544 resolution and a settings file whose lastVersion matches the game (about 73 FPS average, 45 for the 1% low, on a Redmagic Astra 2; the same drive on 0.39.4 gave about 101). On the same tablet Box64 0.4.4-r3 (Performance) gave 27 FPS in its only valid run and failed in most launches (CEF UI crash, a pickup that never moves, corrupt floating point in the game's Lua with STRONGMEM=3); Box64 r4, which the Box64 preset selects, was not tested there. Some launches die at startup (1 of 4 on FEX). After a game version change BeamNG's folder cleanup removes the app's LuaJIT-off extension, so the first launch is slow (several minutes of loading). A GPU device loss that crashed SystemUI was seen during tests. TSO off relaxes x86 memory ordering. Long sessions and other phones are untested.

containers.name: BeamNG 0.39 - Linux, FEX + bionic, no PRoot, 960x544
containers.description: BeamNG 0.39.4 native Linux build, the configuration measured on West Coast: FEX 2610 Performance (TSO off), bionic and direct execution with no PRoot, Vulkan thunks, Turnip driver chosen by the app for the GPU (DD-Turnip v0.1.1 on Adreno 840) for the renderer and the game, native Vulkan output, 960x544 with the app upscaler, post effects and frame generation off, sysmem off, GPU memory 8192 MB. Set BeamNG's own graphics to the Lowest preset with a 960 544 resolution (about 100-110 FPS average on a Redmagic Astra 2 and a Z Fold8 Ultra, 1% lows 50-66) or to the Steam Deck preset (about 50 FPS on both). With 3 traffic cars about 80-90 FPS with 1% lows near 12. The game starts from shared storage. Some launches die at startup (exit 133, a CEF startup race: 3 of about 10 on the Fold, 1 of about 10 on the tablet) and one Fold run froze after a Vulkan transfer-queue error; TSO off relaxes x86 memory ordering. Long sessions are untested.
testedOn: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra (SM-F976B, Android 17), BeamNG 0.39.4

containers.name: Linux, FEX + bionic, no PRoot (experimental)
containers.description: Alien: Isolation, native x86-64 Steam build 4940658, run by Android FEX 2610 directly, with no PRoot around the game; the Steam client stays on the glibc runtime. TSO on (FEX_TSOENABLED=1), as the Performance preset with TSO off left the game waiting on a forked process. The game may sit in a Steam library on shared storage: the Android FEX maps its files without PROT_EXEC, which that noexec storage otherwise refuses. The direct bridge takes the game's legacy libraries (libpcre 3, SDL2_image, libidn, librtmp, libldap and the Heimdal Kerberos libraries) from the Steam Linux Runtime (scout). Turnip sysmem on, Zink over the Android Vulkan thunk, the Turnip driver the app chooses for the GPU (DD-Turnip v0.1.1 on Adreno 840), native Vulkan output, 1280x720. Checked on a RedMagic Astra 2 (Android 16, Adreno 840) on 2026-11-11: the game starts from a Steam library on shared storage and renders its opening scene; gameplay, frame rate and long-session stability are untested. Needs the app build with the Alien: Isolation entry of the direct FEX bridge. The PRoot preset is the fallback.

containers.name: Linux, FEX + bionic, no PRoot (experimental)
containers.description: Dead Island Definitive Edition, native x86-64 Steam build 1837542, run by Android FEX 2610 directly, with no PRoot around the game; the Steam client stays on the glibc runtime. TSO on (FEX_TSOENABLED=1, full x87 precision): with the Performance preset's TSO off the game freezes in its intro cutscene on a RedMagic Astra 2. Turnip sysmem on (needed to avoid rendering artifacts, found by testing on the tablet), Zink over the Android Vulkan thunk, the Turnip driver the app chooses for the GPU (DD-Turnip v0.1.1 on Adreno 840), native Vulkan output, 1280x720 with the fit mode. The game runs without a working Steam API (its Steam IPC is left off). Intro, loading and gameplay checked on a RedMagic Astra 2 (Android 16, Adreno 840): 76 FPS in the first outdoor scene; long-session stability is untested. Needs the app build with the direct FEX bridge for Dead Island and its /tmp path mapping. The PRoot preset is the fallback.

containers.name: Linux, FEX + bionic, no PRoot, 8 cores (experimental)
containers.description: Counter-Strike 2, native x86-64 Steam Linux build 26445667, run by Android FEX 2610 directly with no PRoot; the Steam client stays on the glibc runtime. Direct FEX bridge with TSO emulation, the Turnip driver the app chooses for the GPU (DD-Turnip v0.1.1 on Adreno 840), native Vulkan output, native screen size with the window zoomed to the game (fullscreenStretched=2), all 8 cores.
